title: Acme Analytics QBR - platform reliability + streaming issues
next_steps: Redwood to share request-id based RCA for stream cutoffs
Customer to test eu-west region as mitigation
transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2025-10-03 17:00 UTC
Duration: 44 min
Attendees: Naomi Feldman (Redwood), Hannah Schmitt (Redwood), Samir Desai (Acme), Kara Vance (Acme)

Summary (auto)
- Customer seeing streaming responses cut off intermittently
- Discussed retry/reconnect behavior and timeouts
- Agreed to exchange request IDs and timeline

Transcript
Naomi Feldman: Cool, thanks for joining. QBR stuff first, then we can dig into the streaming thing you flagged.
Samir Desai: Yeah. So overall latency is fine, but the stream sometimes just… stops. Like mid answer. No error. Our UI sits there.
Hannah Schmitt: When you say stops, do you see the connection close? Or it stays open but no bytes?
Kara Vance: From our side it looks like the socket closes early. Sometimes we get a partial line at the end. It feels like truncated SSE.
Naomi Feldman: Are you hitting Hosted API in us-east?
Samir Desai: Yup, Hosted. us-east. Using the OpenAI compatible endpoint.
Hannah Schmitt: Got it. If you can send 5 to 10 request IDs with timestamps we can correlate edge logs.
Samir Desai: We can do that. It happens more during our morning peak.
Naomi Feldman: In the meantime we can suggest a client-side reconnect + retry on EOF, and we can also look at region failover.
Kara Vance: Sure. Also, we have some corp proxy stuff. Not sure if that matters.
Hannah Schmitt: It might. We’ve seen idle timeout mismatches. We’ll verify.
Naomi Feldman: Ok, next steps: you send request IDs, we’ll report back with what we find, and we’ll propose mitigations.
